findings.title: The shared CLI harness now puts a working `sq` stub on PATH for every CLI test
findings.description:
`cli_environment` unconditionally prepends a stub `sq` to `PATH` for every `run_cli`/`start_background` call. That stub is not a version-only stub: `tests/sq_stub.py` implements `sq runs prune` (deleting `<id>.json` from the runs directory and exiting 0 when the files exist), `sq runs wait` and `sq run`. Before this change, `sq` was whatever the developer's shell had (usually absent), so CLI tests that exercise `sq`-dependent commands saw "sq missing" unless they supplied their own `PATH`. Now the stub shadows it for all of them, so a command like `amoeba prune sq-runs --yes` will actually delete candidate files and exit 0 rather than reporting `PRUNE_INCOMPLETE` for a missing executable.

I did not read `tests/cli/` in this session, so I cannot say whether those tests already override `PATH` (in which case this is harmless) or whether their assertions now mean something different (in which case the suite is green for the wrong reason). Either way, a harness that changes the meaning of every existing CLI test is a shared-fixture change that deserves an explicit check rather than an implicit one. The safer shape is for the stub to be added by the tests that need it, or for `cli_environment` to take the stub directory as an argument.

findings.title: Two mechanisms confirm a launch, and the tracker's is dead code that raises `KeyError`
findings.description:
`LaunchTracker.confirm(entry_id)` sets `self._launches[entry_id].confirmed = True`, which raises `KeyError` for an entry id the tracker never saw. Nothing in `src/amoeba/runner/` calls it: `RunObserver._confirm` (`src/amoeba/runner/observe.py`) mutates the `TrackedLaunch` it already holds (`tracked.confirmed = True`) and never goes through the tracker. Only tests call `LaunchTracker.confirm`.

Two ways to do the same thing, one of which is unreachable from production and fails with an opaque `KeyError` — the "one value, one source" and DRY rules both point at deleting `LaunchTracker.confirm` and keeping a single path (either the observer mutates the handle directly, or the observer asks the tracker to confirm and the tracker raises a named error). Whichever survives should be the only way, so a future caller cannot pick the one that crashes.

findings.title: A journal entry without a run id makes the fault handler raise `KeyError`
findings.description:
`_in_flight_run_ids` does `str(entry.parameters[PARAM_RUN_ID])` for every unresolved `SQ_RUN` entry of the node. `PARAM_RUN_ID` is a *required* key for new `SQ_RUN` entries (`REQUIRED_PARAMETER_KEYS` in `src/amoeba/store/journal_models.py`), but entries journaled before slice 120 carry no run id — that is exactly why `SquadronRunObserver` routes on `PARAM_RUN_ID in entry.parameters` (`src/amoeba/process/observers/sq_run_id.py`).

This runs inside `escalate()`, which is called from the tenant's process-boundary handler (`src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py`, the `except Exception` branch). A `KeyError` raised there escapes the handler that was supposed to isolate the fault, so a legacy entry turns a per-project fault into a process crash. `entry.parameters.get(PARAM_RUN_ID)` with a `isinstance` check (the pattern used in `src/amoeba/runner/observe.py` and `src/amoeba/runner/finish.py`) keeps the same behaviour for well-formed entries and does not raise for the rest.

findings.title: `escalate` can raise a state error inside the handler meant to contain failures
findings.description: `escalate` calls `store.block(...)`, which raises `InvalidTransitionError` if the node's status is one of `BLOCKED_STATUSES` (`src/amoeba/store/_block_writer.py`, `_refuse_if_blocked`). The guard is `store.blocked_state_for(node.id) is None`, which reads the open blocked state rather than the node's status, so the two can disagree in an integrity problem or under a race. Because the call is made from the tenant's `except Exception` branch, such an error propagates out of the tenant tick and out of `ResidentProcess.run` rather than being isolated to the project. The window is narrow (the status/blocked-state pair is written in one transaction by the store), so this is a robustness note rather than a live bug — but the comment "a failing escalation write means a broken store" only covers store failures, not state errors.

findings.title: A launch's parameters are validated twice, and one failure mode lands after the entry is journaled
findings.description: `_launch` calls `build_argv(action.pipeline, run_id, action.params)` purely for its `ValueError` and discards the result — `launch()` then rebuilds the same argv from the journal entry. The discarded call is not dead: it is what makes a bad parameter fail *before* the entry is journaled, as the comment says. But the validation is partial. `build_argv` does not reject an empty pipeline, while `launch()`'s `_text_parameter` does (`src/amoeba/runner/launch.py`), so an empty pipeline journals an entry and then raises `ValueError` from `launch()`, leaving an unresolved entry that no launch will ever satisfy (recovery later closes it as `not_applied`). Extending `build_argv` to reject an empty pipeline closes the gap in one place and keeps the "validate before journaling" promise true.

findings.title: A node stays `RUNNABLE` after a successful run, so any planner will offer it again
findings.description: `finish.record` blocks the node for `FAILED`, `PAUSED`, `ORPHANED` and launch failures, but a `COMPLETED` run leaves the node in `RUNNABLE` status. `ProjectTick._decide` excludes only nodes with an unresolved journal entry, so once the entry is resolved the node is offered to the planners again. With `PRODUCTION_PLANNERS` empty this cannot happen yet, and `finish.py`'s docstring says routing and checkpoint handling arrive with 125/126 — but the deduplication currently lives entirely in the *test* planners (`OncePerNode` in `tests/runner/test_end_to_end.py`, `ProofPlanner` in `tests/runner/crash_entry.py`), not in the Runner. Worth making explicit in the slice design that 125/126 must move "a node whose run completed is not offered again" into the Runner, or the first real planner will double-launch.

findings.title: `ProjectView.link_probes` uses a missing key to mean "not probed"
findings.description: `LinkProbes.results` (`src/amoeba/runner/probes.py`) returns only the links that have been probed, so a planner reading `view.link_probes["cf-1"]` gets a `KeyError` for an unprobed link and `view.link_probes.get("cf-1")` gets `None` for a type that promises `bool`. `Mapping[str, bool]` with an implicit third state is a trap at a trust boundary; `Mapping[str, bool | None]` (or including every known link with `False`/`None` for "not probed") states the contract in the type.

findings.title: `amoeba.runner.tick` imports its sibling through the package, creating an import cycle
findings.description: `from amoeba.runner import finish` resolves the `amoeba.runner` package, which is mid-initialisation when `__init__` imports `factory` → `tenant` → `tick`. It works today only because CPython's `_handle_fromlist` falls back to importing `amoeba.runner.finish` as a submodule when the attribute is not yet bound. `from amoeba.runner.finish import record` removes the reliance on that fallback and makes the dependency explicit.

findings.title: `validate_settings` re-lists field names as strings and covers only three of the bounds
findings.description: The bound names are spelled as a tuple of strings and read with `getattr(settings, name)`, so a renamed field becomes a runtime `AttributeError` rather than a type error. `launch_grace_seconds` and `sq_timeout_seconds` are not checked for positivity even though the other three are, and the values are read in three separate places in the file (`validate_settings`, `partial(poll_run, ...)`, `LinkProbes`). Naming the fields once — or iterating over the dataclass fields with a predicate — keeps the "one definition site" rule.

findings.title: The journal-before-the-side-effect ordering is enforced and asserted
findings.description: `_launch` journals the entry (`store.journal_issue`) before `launch()` starts the child, and `tests/runner/test_tick.py::test_the_entry_is_journaled_before_the_launch_call` asserts it directly by counting unresolved entries at the moment `Popen` is called (`rig.popen.open_entries_at_call == [1]`). The crash proof (`tests/runner/test_crash_recovery.py`) then exercises the four failure windows around that ordering with real `SIGKILL`s and predicates rather than sleeps.

findings.title: The tick budget is checked before every subprocess call site, and the check is mechanical
findings.description: `allows_call` is consulted before the poll (`observe._confirmed`, `observe._unconfirmed`), before each `cf` probe command (`probes.probe_link`), and before `Popen` (`tick._act`). `tests/runner/test_budget_coverage.py` wraps all three call kinds so that a call starting after the deadline fails the test, which is the property the project wants enforced rather than asserted in prose.
